verdicts.flaw_description: Rainfall is a live alternative cause that reaches every unit: "Rainfall in each block's season ran to roughly double the year before, and every block lay in open ground, taking rain as it fell." Double the rain on open-ground maize explains the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gain over the previous summer just as well as the drip line does.

Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before the boxes went up: case one was "boxed 3 June" but counted "by 27 March", and case three was "boxed 2 November" but counted "by 24 September". Those fledging counts cannot have been produced by boxes installed months after the count date.

The confounder reaches the units: "Class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group." Because English was taught to the whole class, the halved roll halved the group size in the very lessons being measured, so smaller classes explain the 5-9 point comprehension gain over the previous autumn term.

The pass rates cover a narrower population than the claim: "Pass rates cover the students who attended every block, and about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block." Roughly 25% of each cohort is dropped from the figures, so the 4-8 point gain is for a self-selected full-attendance subgroup compared against whole-cohort prior-term rates.
